passages.text: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.
passages.sermon:
God spoke in the past.
He spoke many times.
He spoke in many different ways.
He spoke to our ancestors.
He spoke through the prophets.
passages.original: Πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ Θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις

passages.text: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.
passages.sermon:
God has spoken to us in these last days.
He spoke by His Son.
God appointed His Son as heir of all things.
God made the universe through His Son.
passages.original: ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τῶν ἡμερῶν τούτων ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν Υἱῷ ὃν ἔθηκεν κληρονόμον πάντων δι’ οὗ καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς αἰῶνας

passages.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
passages.sermon:
The Son shows God’s glory.
The Son exactly represents God’s nature.
The Son upholds everything by His powerful word.
The Son provided purification for sins.
After this, the Son sat at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven.
passages.original: ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ φέρων τε τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως δι’ αὐτοῦ καθαρισμὸν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ποιησάμενος ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τῆς Μεγαλωσύνης ἐν ὑψηλοῖς

passages.text: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
God appointed Jesus as heir of all things.
God made the universe through Jesus.
Jesus became far greater than the angels.
Jesus received a name much better than the names of the angels.
His name shows His greatness over them.
passages.original: τοσούτῳ κρείττων γενόμενος τῶν ἀγγέλων ὅσῳ διαφορώτερον παρ’ αὐτοὺς κεκληρονόμηκεν ὄνομα

passages.text: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son”?
passages.sermon:
God never said these words to any angel.
God said, “You are My Son.”
God also said, “Today I have become Your Father.”
God said again, “I will be His Father.”
God said, “He will be My Son.”
God spoke these words about the Son, not about any angel.
passages.original: Τίνι γὰρ εἶπέν ποτε τῶν ἀγγέλων Υἱός μου εἶ σύ ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε Καὶ πάλιν Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς Πατέρα καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι εἰς Υἱόν

passages.text: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”
passages.sermon:
God has a firstborn Son.
God brings His firstborn Son into the world.
God speaks about His firstborn Son.
God commands all His angels.
God says, “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ πάλιν εἰσαγάγῃ τὸν πρωτότοκον εἰς τὴν οἰκουμένην λέγει Καὶ προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι Θεοῦ

passages.text: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”
passages.sermon: God speaks about the angels.\r\nGod says, “He makes His angels winds.”\r\nGod also says, “He makes His servants flames of fire.”
passages.original: Καὶ πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀγγέλους λέγει Ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα

passages.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His Son.
God calls the Son “God.”
God says the Son’s throne lasts forever and ever.
God says the Son rules with justice.
Justice is the scepter of the Son’s kingdom.
passages.original: Πρὸς δὲ τὸν Υἱόν Ὁ θρόνος σου ὁ Θεὸς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος τῆς εὐθύτητος ῥάβδος τῆς βασιλείας σου

passages.text: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”
passages.sermon:
The Son loves righteousness.
The Son hates wickedness.
God is the God of the Son.
God has anointed the Son.
God used the oil of joy to anoint the Son.
God set the Son above His companions.
passages.original: ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀνομίαν διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέν σε ὁ Θεός ὁ Θεός σου ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου

passages.text: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
passages.sermon:
The Son is the Lord.
The Lord existed in the beginning.
The Lord laid the foundations of the earth.
The Lord made the heavens.
The heavens are the work of the Lord’s hands.
passages.original: Καί Σὺ κατ’ ἀρχάς Κύριε τὴν γῆν ἐθεμελίωσας καὶ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σού εἰσιν οἱ οὐρανοί

passages.text: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.
passages.sermon: Created things will perish.\r\nYou, Lord, will remain.\r\nAll created things will wear out like a garment.
passages.original: αὐτοὶ ἀπολοῦνται σὺ δὲ διαμένεις καὶ πάντες ὡς ἱμάτιον παλαιωθήσονται

passages.text: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”
passages.sermon:
God is eternal.
God does not change.
God will roll up the heavens like a robe.
God will change the heavens like a garment.
God always stays the same.
God’s years never end.
passages.original: καὶ ὡσεὶ περιβόλαιον ἑλίξεις αὐτούς ὡς ἱμάτιον καὶ ἀλλαγήσονται σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ καὶ τὰ ἔτη σου οὐκ ἐκλείψουσιν

passages.text: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”?
passages.sermon:
God never said these words to any angel.
God said, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
God spoke these words to His Son, not to angels.
God gave this honor and authority to Jesus Christ alone.
passages.original: Πρὸς τίνα δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἴρηκέν ποτε Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου

passages.text: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?
passages.sermon:
Angels are spirits.
Angels serve God.
God sends angels to help people.
These people will inherit salvation.
Angels are ministering spirits.
God sends them to serve those who will receive salvation.
passages.original: Οὐχὶ πάντες εἰσὶν λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα εἰς διακονίαν ἀποστελλόμενα διὰ τοὺς μέλλοντας κληρονομεῖν σωτηρίαν
